FirstCry, the largest name in the list, grew a modest 13% in Q1 FY27 and is still loss-making; most other baby/kids brands in the sheet had no recent public signal.

Redseer projects online BPC growth of 36-39% in CY2026, helped by quick commerce and Tier 2+ demand. In this list, Nykaa, Honasa/Mamaearth, Plum, Minimalist and Foxtale are still expanding, though SUGAR, WOW Skin Science and Myglamm show stress.

New category for D2C bicycles and e-cycles (EMotorad, SVITCH, Motovolt, Nexzu, OMObikes, Ninety One, Rowwet). New category, currently only Kalakaram (DIY kits, Shark Tank India). Imagimake and ToyKraftt, which also sell craft kits, were grouped under Toys & Games. No recent public financials were found.

Lenskart remains the category standout after its 2025 IPO: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32.5% to ₹2,845 Cr and profit more than doubled. ClearDekho was added as a value Tier III/IV player, with no recent public financials in this pass.
Zouk's FY25 revenue rose 62% to ₹127 Cr, and DailyObjects raised ₹332 Cr in a Series C in Oct 2026.

Redseer notes fashion is growing, especially in Tier 2+, but outcomes in this list are mixed: Snitch, The Souled Store, Rare Rabbit and Blissclub are scaling, Fabindia and Manyavar are roughly flat, and Clovia's FY25 revenue fell.

New category covering puja products, handmade gifts and festive decor (Bigsmall, ExclusiveLane, My Pooja Box, Nirmalaya and others). No recent public financials or a 2026 sector report were found, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.

Inc42 says F&B is the largest funded Indian D2C segment (about one-third of funded D2C startups; nearly $3 Bn since 2015), favoured for repeat purchases. Licious, The Whole Truth, Yoga Bar, Blue Tokai and Vahdam posted strong recent growth; Happilo's FY25 revenue declined. This pass added meat, snack and bakery brands; Eggoz's FY26 revenue rose 39% to ₹180 Cr, and Potful was named to Inc42 FAST42 2026.

Public data is limited, but mid-premium D2C labels are still adding capital and stores: Bacca Bucci's FY25 revenue rose 22%, and Neeman's raised $4 Mn in Jan 2026, saying it was on track for ~₹180 Cr FY26 revenue.
New category for Indian PC-gaming peripheral brands (Ant Esports, Cosmic Byte). No brand-level public financials were confirmed in this pass, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.

New category for indoor-plant D2C brands (Kyari, Nurturing Green), kept separate from the older Home & Garden pair (Ugaoo, Nurserylive). Both new brands appeared on Shark Tank India; no recent audited financials were confirmed in this pass.

Inc42 flags supplements, wellness and functional nutrition as core D2C 3.0 categories. HealthKart, Kapiva, Traya, Oziva, Wellbeing Nutrition and Mosaic Wellness (Man Matters/Be Bodywise) all showed strong recent revenue or funding signals.

Redseer lists home and furniture among categories carrying 2026 online-retail momentum, but brand results are split: Wakefit and The Sleep Company grew, while Pepperfry (down round) and Urban Ladder (shrinking product sales) struggled.
Only two brands (Ugaoo, Nurserylive) are in the list, and no recent public financial or funding signal was found, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.

Three brands are now in this list. Longway ranked #2 on Inc42 FAST42 2026 and DrinkPrime was also named to that list (FY23–FY25 CAGR). Airth, an AC air-purifier brand, was added in this pass with no recent public financials. No separate 2026 sector report was used.
New category for toxin-free / bamboo home-care brands (Koparo, Bamboo India). Both are Unclear on brand-level growth, so the category is marked Stable pending better public data.

Digital-first jewellery is still scaling. BlueStone's FY26 revenue rose 38% to ₹2,441 Cr with its first full-year profit; Giva, Palmonas and Titan-owned CaratLane also reported expansion or fresh funding.

New category in this list. The Indus Valley raised $17 Mn in June 2026, and Cüraa raised ₹40 Cr Series A in August 2026 (the company said monthly net revenue had grown 25x since its September 2024 launch). Other cookware brands in the sheet were Unclear.
Bombay Shaving Company and Beardo posted sharp FY26 revenue and profit improvement; The Man Company was roughly flat with wider losses, and Ustraa's FY25 revenue declined.

New category for camping, trekking and motorcycle travel gear (Tripole, Guardian Gears, Adventure Worx). Wildcraft remains under Travel & Luggage from the earlier list. No recent public financials were found, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.
New category with two party-decor brands (PartyPropz, The Balloonwala). No recent public financials or a 2026 sector report were found.
Inc42 cites premium pet care as a D2C 3.0 micro-category; Supertails' FY25 revenue rose 68% to ₹108 Cr (losses also widened). Other pet brands in the list lacked recent public filings in this pass.
New category for Indian motorcycle riding-gear brands. ViaTerra's FY25 revenue rose ~43.5% to ₹15.7 Cr (bootstrapped); Rynox had no recent public financials beyond Tracxn's sub-₹10 Cr estimate.

New category with four D2C brands (That Sassy Thing, MyMuse, Nooky, Nuutjob). Bold Care remains under Health & Wellness from the earlier list. No recent public financials were found for the new brands, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.
New category with two Indian connected-home brands (Oakter, IFITech). No audited 2025-26 financials were confirmed in this pass, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.

New category for home-gym equipment and sports-tech brands (Cockatoo, Aroleap, Protoner, PowerMax, Str8bat, Skate Supply India and Hashtag Fitness). No recent public financials or a 2026 sector report were found, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.

New category in this list. PlayShifu's FY25 operating revenue rose 27.3% to ₹110 Cr; Mirana Toys raised ₹57.5 Cr in a Nov 2025 Series A, and Legend of Toys raised ₹21 Cr in May 2026. Most other toy brands here had no recent public financials.
Evidence is thin outside Mokobara, which is raising a ₹91 Cr Series C at about 2.8x its prior valuation after nearly doubling FY25 revenue to ₹230 Cr.
New category, currently only Sylvi (Surat-based D2C fashion watches). No recent public financials were found.

New in this pass: home air-purifier, humidifier and water-filter brands sold D2C (Mila, Rabbit Air, Canopy, Clearly Filtered, LARQ). Molekule was excluded as defunct. No recent category-level figure was confirmed.

D2C-plus-retail auto accessories and car care (WeatherTech, TuxMat, Chemical Guys, Crutchfield) are included. Marketplace-style truck-part retailers were excluded. No recent category financials were used.

Adobe projects holiday 2026 baby-product online sales 113% above average September levels during Cyber Week, but that is a seasonal spike, not a full-year rate. The Honest Company's FY2025 revenue fell 1.9% and 2026 reported revenue is guided down 16–18% after category exits; most other baby/kids brands here are Unclear.

eMarketer says food and beverage will propel US ecommerce in 2026, while holiday data also shows cosmetics among the faster categories: Adobe projects online cosmetics up about 10% in holiday 2026. e.l.f. Adobe expects holiday 2026 online electronics sales of $63.3B, up 5.9%. Peloton's Q4 FY2025 sales were down ~6% but FY2026 was guided at $2.4–$2.5B with $320M FY2025 free cash flow; other connected-fitness and gadget brands here are mostly Unclear.
Cricut is the public anchor in this small group, alongside Knit Picks and Purl Soho. No FY2025/FY2026 Cricut figure was used in this pass.
Warby Parker, the anchor brand, reported FY2025 revenue of $872M, up 13.0%. Other online eyewear brands in the list had no recent public filings in this pass.
Accessory-led brands such as Baggu, Cuyana, Ridge and Pela are broken out separately from apparel and luggage, and no recent public financials were found for them.

Adobe expects US holiday 2026 online apparel sales of $51.3B, up 4.7%. In this list, Quince, FIGS, Rent the Runway and workwear brand BRUNT show clear growth, Lululemon is only modestly up with lower operating profit, and many digitally native apparel brands have no recent public filings.
Farm-direct and on-demand florists (UrbanStems, The Bouqs, Farmgirl Flowers) plus gift brands (Uncommon Goods) are now grouped here. No recent category-level financials were used.

eMarketer (Mar 2026) says food and beverage will be the main engine of a US ecommerce rebound through 2030. Adobe also projects holiday 2026 online grocery up about 10% to $26.1B. Meat snacks, candy and other shelf-stable snacks are now broken out in a separate Snacks & Meat Snacks tab row.
The category is mixed. Allbirds' FY2025 revenue fell 19.7% and it agreed in Mar 2026 to sell brand/IP for ~$39M, while many other D2C footwear labels in the list have no recent public filings.
Houseplant and seed D2C (The Sill, Bloomscape, Lettuce Grow, Johnny's) is established online, but no reliable 2025–2026 category growth figure was confirmed in this pass.

Hims & Hers' FY2025 revenue rose 59% to $2.3B, and the category is subscription-friendly. Broader US ecommerce commentary still treats wellness/supplements as a resilient online vertical, though most private supplement brands in this list are Unclear.

Premium artificial-tree DTC (Balsam Hill, King of Christmas, Treetopia) is a large seasonal online category, but no reliable full-year 2025–2026 category growth figure was confirmed in this pass, and unsourced market-share estimates were not used.

Adobe forecasts holiday 2026 online furniture sales up 7.3% to $33.4B, but mattress DTC is weaker: Purple's latest-year revenue fell 3.9% with a -9.2% operating margin, and Casper remains private after its 2022 take-private with no recent public figures.

Adobe expects household cleaning to rise 49% vs average September sales during Cyber Week, but that is seasonal. No full-year 2026 category financials were used, and brands such as Blueland, Grove and Tru Earth are Unclear at the brand level.

The list includes Mejuri, Gorjana, Kendra Scott and online diamond retailers, but no reliable 2025–2026 category-level ecommerce growth figure was confirmed in this pass, and brand-level filings were not reviewed in depth.

New grill, coffee-equipment and appliance brands (Traeger, Blackstone, Fellow, Mill, Lomi) are listed here. Earlier cookware entries such as Made In, HexClad, Caraway and Our Place remain under Home & Furniture so historical rows were not rewritten. Traeger is public; no FY2025/FY2026 figure was used.
Harry's, Dollar Shave Club and Dr. Squatch are established, but no recent public brand-level growth figures were found in this pass (Harry's is inside Edgewell; DSC is inside Unilever).

This group covers fire pits, coolers, camp stoves and ultralight gear (Solo Stove, BioLite, RTIC, NEMO, Big Agnes). Yeti remains in Travel & Luggage. No recent category-level ecommerce figure was used.
Online party and invitation specialists (Oriental Trading, Shindigz, Basic Invite) are included. Party City-style mall retail was not added. No recent category financials were used.

NA D2C and omnichannel brands (Dame, Maude, We-Vibe, Foria, OhNut) are listed. No reliable recent category-level ecommerce figure was used.

Protein snacks sit inside the broader grocery/F&B online upswing, but the only public brand newly added here, Stryve (OTC: SNAX), expected roughly flat FY2025 revenue, a still-negative net loss, a strategic-alternatives review, and a January 2026 production halt after plant damage. Most other snack brands are Unclear.

Golf (Newton Golf, formerly Sacks Parente; L.A.B. Golf; PXG), pickleball (Selkirk), ergs (Concept2) and garage-gym brands are grouped here. Rogue and REP remain under Consumer Electronics. Seed Golf was excluded as Ireland-founded.
Notebook, planner and desk brands (Ugmonk, Field Notes, Rifle Paper Co., Erin Condren, Grovemade) are grouped here. No 2025–2026 category figure was confirmed.

Meal kits and single-product subscriptions stay under their product categories. No recent category-level figure was confirmed, so the trend is Unclear.

True D2C power-tool specialists are scarce versus traditional trade brands. This group is mostly hand tools, woodworking and multi-tools (Lee Valley, Lie-Nielsen, Tekton, Leatherman, Woodpeckers, Kreg). No category-level 2026 figure was used.

Adobe's holiday 2026 forecast pegs US online toy sales at about $9.6B, up roughly 10%. This new group includes KiwiCo, Magna-Tiles, Melissa & Doug and game studios such as Exploding Kittens; Lovevery remains listed under Baby & Kids. No brand-level FY2025/FY2026 figures were used here.

Yeti, the largest public brand in this group, posted FY2025 revenue of $1.9B, up just 2.1%, with operating profit down 13%. Away, Monos, Béis and others lack recent public financials, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.

e-Conomy SEA 2025 (Google, Temasek, Bain) projects SEA ecommerce GMV of about US$185B in 2025, up 16% from US$156B; video commerce is now ~25% of ecommerce GMV vs under 5% in 2022, so many D2C brands sell through TikTok Shop and live commerce alongside their own sites.
Falling birth rates shrink home markets (CNA, on Singapore baby-care brands), so winners expand abroad: Hegen grew to 28 markets in 2026 with plans for 35, and Singapore is only 6–7% of its revenue.

Indonesia beauty ecommerce grew ~27% in 2025 to about IDR 137T, with TikTok Shop share rising from 17% (2023) to 37% (2025). Sociolla revenue rose ~71% in 2025 and Cocoon began exporting to Japan, but competition is intense: Somethinc was reported weighing a sale in Feb 2026.
Local gaming-peripheral and audio brands (Rexus, Nubwo, FATfreq, Prism+) sell D2C and via retail; no recent public financials found in this pass.
D2C eyewear with home try-on and owned stores is expanding: Saturdays raised US$6.3M (Jan 2026) and Sunnies Studios entered Thailand in 2025 and added more stores in 2026.

Vietnamese local fashion is moving online even as stores close: YouNet reports local brands led online fashion in H1 2025, with Coolmate top in men's fashion ecommerce. Coolmate closed a Series C (Nov 2025), Yuedpao revenue rose ~32% in 2025 and Love, Bonito reached EBITDA break-even; Pomelo is mixed.

App-first coffee is scaling fast: Kopi Kenangan's 2025 revenue rose 45% to US$184M with H1 2026 up 62%, and Fore Coffee's FY2025 revenue rose 44%. Craft chocolate and specialty-coffee roasters in this list are mostly private and Unclear.

Indonesian and Vietnamese local sneaker labels (Compass, Ventela, Patrobas, NAH Project, Ananas) are popular via drops and marketplaces, but none publish financials, so no category-level growth figure was found in this pass.

Femcare and personal-care devices are attracting growth capital: Blood (period care) raised a Series B (Feb 2025) and is in 7,000+ doors, and Stryv raised US$11.5M Series B (Oct 2026). Lunio is also expanding into recovery and ergonomics.

Mixed. Online mattress brands are drawing capital (Lunio parent Horizon raised US$12.5M, Nov 2026, citing the shift of mattresses and furniture online), while Castlery guided FY2026 growth to flat or single digits due to tariffs and supply-chain costs.
Mostly small private brands (Carrie K., Mondays Made, Bloomthis, FlowerStore.ph, Rags2Riches, Tulisan); no recent public financials found in this pass.

Vertex says Lunio is the leading D2C sleep brand in Thailand and Taiwan and that SEA mattress/furniture buying is shifting online. Many mattress-in-a-box brands are in this list (Woosa, Noah, Origin, Sonno, Sommni, Ru9, Mimpi, TURU).

Indonesia's modest-fashion consumption was about US$20B in 2024, growing roughly 18% a year, and ecommerce is a key channel. Most brands here (Buttonscarves, Naelofar, dUCk, Poplook and others) are private with no public financials, so individual signals are Unclear.

The SEA pet-food market is estimated at ~US$2.8B in 2025 with ~11% annual growth; 46% of owners in ID, PH, TH and VN buy pet supplies online, and Thai online pet-food sales were projected up ~20% in 2025, with fresh and human-grade food gaining.
Small set of homegrown educational/collectible toy brands (Mighty Jaxx, SparksMag, Little Friends, Dev Depot, Happy Story Co.); no category growth data found in this pass.

World Wide Worx forecasts SA online retail at R159bn in 2026, up 22.5% on 2025, reaching 10% of total retail for the first full year. 79.1% of adults have internet access but only 34.2% shop online, so there is still room to grow.
Children's toys are bought by 13.7% of online shoppers (World Wide Worx 2026 via V8 Media), but local baby and toy brands are small, handmade-led businesses with no public growth data.

Brand-level evidence only. Sealand Gear opened its 11th store and moved to a larger production facility in 2026, and SakSak reached cult status in about a year with a ~17% repeat-buyer rate (V8 Media).

Clicks raised its stake in premium beauty retailer ARC to 61% in 2026, calling it a faster-growing segment. Mordor projects SA cosmetics and personal care rising from ~$4.2bn (2026) to ~$5.97bn by 2032. In this list Love Kinks, Lelive, Skin Functional, Swiitch and Hermosa Flor show growth signals.

Small local categories. Gifts are bought by 16% of online shoppers, but no category growth data is available. Eyewear is mostly Cape Town sunglasses labels, and tech accessories are led by Volkano and Peachz.

Clothing has the most online buyers but grows slowly. Shein (21.5% of online shoppers) and Temu still compete hard, though Shein growth slowed to 11% in 2025 after SARS ended the small-parcel duty concession.

Faithful to Nature, an online natural-products retailer, has grown revenue at ~33% CAGR over three years and reached 15 stores by Sep 2026. Collagen, women's health and period care brands are proliferating.

Home is one of the faster categories: Woolworths Home +14.0% and TFG homeware and furniture +8.7% (company results compiled by V8 Media). Litehouse scaled to 8-figure revenue on its own Shopify store, and online-only mattress brands (Sloom, Meelu, SleepSport, Fast Asleep) compete on 100-night trials.

TFG reported jewellery sales up 3.9%, in line with clothing. Most SA jewellery labels in this list are small studios with no public financials. Pichulik keeps launching collections and collaborations.
Yuppiechef (Mr Price Group) posted double-digit sales growth and market-share gains in FY2026, and growth continued in H1 to Sep 2026 across online and physical stores.

Black-owned natural haircare brands are moving from Instagram-led D2C into national pharmacy retail: Love Kinks launched in 87 Clicks stores across five countries in Oct 2025 and raised funding in Apr 2026.

The SA pet market grew 15.8% in 2025 vs 3.7% for overall retail (Eighty20). Woolworths bought Absolute Pets and Checkers grew Petshop Science to 185 stores. D2C brands in this list focus on raw, insect-protein and personalised food.

Fieldbar (premium cooler boxes) topped the News24 / Statista fastest-growing companies list in Apr 2026 with ~1,600% growth and R134m revenue in 2024. Local overlanding, camping and home-gym makers sell direct online.

Euromonitor projects Middle East and Africa beauty to grow 14% in 2026, to USD 55.7 billion, helped by local ingredients, climate-specific skincare and the rise of Arab Beauty. This list includes 39 beauty brands, from Huda Beauty and izil Beauty to Turkish and Egyptian independents; most are private and unmarked on growth.

Euromonitor expects MEA fragrances, the cornerstone of regional beauty, to grow 12% in 2026 to USD 9.0 billion, supported by oud, scent-stacking rituals and tourist demand. This list has 12 fragrance houses with their own e-commerce sites, including Swiss Arabian, Rasasi, Ajmal, Lattafa, Arabian Oud and Kayali.

Fashion is the largest online category in the UAE. EZDubai/Euromonitor put UAE e-commerce at AED 42.2 billion in 2025, with apparel and footwear the biggest slice at AED 11.4 billion. AMC also notes fashion had more than 21% of UAE e-commerce in 2025. This list has 31 fashion brands (activewear, bags, ready-to-wear); most have no public financials.

Premium modest wear is a named demand driver in GCC online fashion. In this list, Saudi on-demand abaya platform Aya raised a $7M Series A in 2026, and Leem expanded into a UK flagship, Selfridges and New York Fashion Week in 2025. Mordor Intelligence estimates the Middle East and Africa coffee market at USD 17.14 billion in 2026, with a 7.75% CAGR to 2031. This list has 18 food and drink brands, including Dubai roaster RAW Coffee, several GCC specialty roasters, and date and chocolate brands such as Tamrah, Bateel, The Date Room and Mirzam. Brand-level public financials are scarce.

AMC notes that GCC gifting, including jewellery, sees sharp festive spikes (it cites historically very large floral GMV jumps in peak windows, with jewellery named alongside confectionery and flowers). This list has 14 regional jewellery brands with official stores, mostly private UAE and Saudi labels, plus Azza Fahmy and Alexa Fine Jewelry. No brand-level 2026 financials were found.

AMC says the GCC floral category has historically seen around 132% GMV growth in peak festive windows, and that gifting more broadly surges around Ramadan and Eid (regional e-commerce up 30-50% in Ramadan). This list currently has only Floward as a dedicated flower e-commerce brand, plus a few gift/homeware labels in other categories.

The category is thin in this list (Eyewa and Karen Wazen), but Eyewa, the main regional D2C-origin eyewear brand, raised a $100M Series C in November 2024 and later reported 200 GCC stores (August 2025).

Nine home, furniture, linen and décor brands are in the list (including Jordan's Silsal, Egypt's ariika, Turkey's WellMatt and UAE's DunePine). No 2026 category-wide public report with usable figures was found in this pass, and the brands themselves are mostly private.

Only Eliksir is in the list as a clear own-brand UAE supplements D2C. Multi-brand retailers such as Sporter were excluded. No recent public category financials for regional D2C supplements were found in this pass.
The list has only Touches, a UAE pet-furniture brand. Multi-brand pet retailers were excluded. No 2026 regional D2C pet-care report was found in this pass.

Supplement and nutrition brands show strong growth signals: Huel's FY to Jul 2025 revenue rose 18.6% to £253.8M and Danone completed its ~€1bn takeover, and Free Soul reported £42M sales in the year to Apr 2026 and ranked 10th in the 2026 Sunday Times 100. Most other brands in the category are Unclear.

Split picture. Gousto's FY2025 revenue rose 9.9% to £342.9M with a third profitable year, but HelloFresh's Q3 2026 revenue fell 9.8%, Naked Wines' FY26 revenue fell 20%, and BrewDog entered administration in Mar 2026 before a ~£33M rescue deal.

Thin evidence. Emma Sleep's 2025 revenue was below its 2024 level of €845M (another decline) while profit hit a record high, per its owner. Other home and furniture brands in the list had no recent public financials in this pass.

Hardware-led D2C brands are scaling: Oura's first nine months of 2026 revenue was $1.21B, up 74%, and Nothing passed $2B in lifetime revenue by May 2026 while expanding its phone line. Other brands in this category have no recent public figures.

Only one data point: Daniel Wellington's 2025 sales fell 10% to SEK 750M per Breakit, and the brand is now owned by Timex. Other jewellery and watch brands in the list had no recent public financials in this pass.
Moonpig Group's FY to Apr 2026 revenue rose 6.5% to £373.0M, a modest but steady gain. Other flower, gift and personalised-card brands in the list have no recent public figures.

tonies' Q3 2026 revenue rose 27.6% year on year to €179.9M and it reiterated its FY26 estimates. Other toy and game brands in the list (Games Workshop, Mantic Games, Rex London and others) had no recent public financials in this pass.

Direct bike brands are under pressure: Canyon's 2025 revenue fell ~7% to €738M with a third straight year of losses, and Cowboy went bankrupt and was rescued by ReBirth Group in Dec 2025 with more than €45M of debt wiped. Small sample of five brands.
